text:
Seirei Academy was holding its first-ever Christmas party, organized by student council officer Yuki Suou. Out on the gymnasium floor, two pairs of election candidates were already midway through the first dance.

“Ooh…”

“Ahh…”

Gentle music drifted from the stage speakers as voices of admiration rose from the students standing by the walls, watching the two pairs dance beautifully.

Naturally, Alisa was the one everyone noticed first. Her trademark silver hair had been pinned up in a way that made her look more sophisticated. In a gown that showed off her mysterious beauty and exceptional figure, she looked every bit like a princess from a foreign land.

With every graceful spin, her silver hair swayed and her flawless pale skin shimmered under the lights. The dreamlike scene left many of the students, boys and girls alike, staring at her as though their souls had been taken from them.

But as the dance went on, a few students who knew more about dancing began to notice the way she moved.

“Hey, doesn't Kujou-san's footwork kind of stand out to you?”

“Yeah… it’s kind of hard to explain. It’s like she’s moving too fast into each step… Does that make sense? You could say she’s light on her feet, but…”

Alisa had been holding back the more eye-catching dancing she’d shown at last year’s school festival afterparty so she wouldn’t steal the spotlight at Yuki’s dance party. Even then, she couldn’t completely suppress the habits that had been ingrained in her from practicing ballet since childhood. They still showed through in the way she danced, most noticeably in how pronounced her sideways steps tended to be.

Ordinarily, Alisa’s distinctive movements and footwork would have drawn much more attention for all the wrong reasons, especially with Yuki’s pair dancing right beside them in what looked like proper ballroom dancing. Even so, Masachika’s skill as her partner kept the dance graceful and well put together.

“…Watching her now, Kujou-san really lets loose when she dances, doesn’t she?” one student commented.

“Her partner’s impressive, keeping the rhythm steady even with her dancing like that.”

Another student nodded. “He makes it look easy… but not just anyone could pull that off. That guy’s really something else.”

One after another, students’ eyes began drifting toward Masachika.

“Kuze-kun isn't from some upper-class family or anything, right? Considering that, he's pretty… no wait, he's actually really good at dancing, isn't he?”

“He’s obviously talented, but he isn’t even trying to show off. Instead, he just matches his partner. Kinda impressive, isn’t it?”

“Tell me about it. It’s always the good dancers who end up doing their own thing out there, and the worst ones start trying to tell you how to dance.”

“If it was with him, though… I think I’d actually want to dance.”

Some of the students were openly impressed by Masachika’s dancing, while others began watching him with growing interest.

The students looked on at Alisa and Masachika with a mix of admiration and respect. Yuki, meanwhile, watched the pair from the corner of her eye as she danced.

As expected of Onii-chan… There’s no way he’s this good just because he used to dance. I’m sure he practiced beforehand, but still… you’ve gotta hand it to him.

Yuki and her partner, Ayano, were drawing attention too, but for an entirely different reason than Alisa and Masachika. Surprisingly, though, it wasn’t the party’s host who had everyone looking their way... it was Ayano, and one glance at the pair made it obvious why.

“Oh, how wonderful…!”

“Is this what it means to think something is too precious…?”

All around them came excited sighs, carrying a different kind of energy from the reactions Alisa and Masachika had drawn.

“This expressionless butler and young lady pairing… it’s so moe…!”

This time, Ayano wasn’t in a dress or a maid outfit. She was dressed as a butler and taking the male role in the dance.

She’d braided her long black hair down her back, and the hidden lifts in her boots made her even taller than Yuki, giving her the look of a calm, composed butler dressed in men’s clothing. With Ayano leading her, Yuki came across as a devoted, hardworking young lady carrying the weight of her family name all on her own. Ayano’s heartfelt words about Yuki at the closing ceremony only reinforced that impression.

“Why do those two make me feel all warm and fuzzy inside?”

“Ahh~ it’s like my heart’s being purified.”

“Ugh… they’re shining way too brightly…”

People looked at Alisa and Masachika the way fans looked up to their idols. With Yuki and Ayano, though, the feeling was a little closer to home, and people found themselves wanting to cheer them on.

Yuki knew exactly what kind of reaction they were getting, and she couldn’t help but smile to herself.

Heh heh heh. Come on, you want to cheer us on, don’t you? We’re just too lovable, aren’t we? Could you really bring yourself to let a pair with a bond this strong lose?

Yuki hadn’t expected Ayano to say what she did at the closing ceremony. But seeing how it had all turned out, she had to give Ayano credit.

Up to that point, most of Yuki’s support had come from the trust she’d earned as the perfect young lady and as the former middle-school student council president everyone knew they could rely on. People supported her almost by default, with the simple thought, You can’t go wrong with Suou-san.

But Ayano’s open and earnest declaration of her feelings as Yuki’s childhood friend and attendant had unexpectedly cracked that image of perfection, making the crowd think, We need to support her!

That was something Yuki could never have managed on her own, not while keeping up the refined young lady act that had earned her the nickname .

People are drawn more to stories than facts or achievements… The president won his election the same way. The students were drawn to the story of an overweight, gloomy student reaching for someone far out of his league, and that was what ultimately won him the election.

As Yuki turned gracefully, she looked over at Masachika and Alisa. Objectively, the two of them looked like a beautiful girl paired with an ordinary guy, but somehow, they still looked good together.

Still…

A boy and a girl joining forces to take on the election together. There’s certainly something beautiful about that too… but a pairing like that inevitably comes with at least some jealousy and people reading too much into it. Compared to two girls who’ve been childhood friends, supporting each other every step of the way, which pair would people support more wholeheartedly?

Alisa was happily dancing with Masachika, a softer smile than usual on her face. Seeing just how unguarded and carefree she looked, Yuki snorted to herself.

Well, well… look at you, taking it easy and enjoying yourself. You sure you can afford that, Alya-san? Keep this up, and I’ll be the one winning everyone over at this party.

There was one thing worth keeping in mind. Yuki herself was the one behind the Christmas party, and naturally, she had more than a few ways prepared to secure an advantage in the election.

Really, Alya-san. You just never learn to keep your guard up, do you?

Seeing Alisa’s happy, completely unguarded face, Yuki… Yuki was…

…Annoyed★

For some reason, a sudden rush of irritation came over her.

Yuki was suddenly hit with the urge to slip into little-sister mode right then and drive a loving dropkick into her brother’s back. Before she knew it, her grip on Ayano’s hand had tightened.

“Yuki-sama…?” Ayano murmured, puzzled, and it snapped Yuki back to herself.

“It’s nothing,” Yuki faced forward again and answered quietly. The irritation was still there, though, and she knew exactly what was causing it.

We'll all work together on the student council and create a system where everyone can aim to join the Raikoukai, huh?

The pledge Alisa had made earlier at the closing ceremony was what had Yuki so irritated. It was bold enough to take her aback, grand enough to make her scoff, and so idealistic it sounded almost like a dream.

…Hmph.

She didn’t like it. Not one bit. And in that moment, something else became clear. This wasn’t the kind of feeling she’d ever have toward someone beneath her.

Yeah… I admit it, Alya-san. You really are someone worth competing against for student council president.

She finally acknowledged Alisa as more than just Masachika’s partner, seeing her as an equal she would have to give everything she had to beat. And precisely because she now saw her that way…

After making a pledge like that, you’re already getting all lovestruck with your head in the clouds. I’ll have to make sure this party leaves you with the feeling of defeat firmly etched into you…

A defiant smile crept across Yuki’s face as the song came to an end, bringing the first dance to a close… and with that, the real party began.

The first dance between the two pairs had come to an end, and though it felt like hours had passed, less than five minutes had actually gone by. A moment later, thunderous applause erupted seemingly out of nowhere, and cheers rained down on the four standing in the center of the gymnasium.

“Whooooa! That was incredible!!!”

“Just seeing this made the trip worth it…!”

“Kujou-san looks absolutely gorgeous! She’s like a princess!”

“Suou-san was incredible! Just perfect!”

“Ayano-chan’s so cool! And she’s sooo cuuute!!!”

“Kuze! You were awesome!”

With the applause and cheers still not letting up, the four bowed to the students around them, then each pair stepped away in different directions.

After spotting Touya, Chisaki and Maria in the crowd, Masachika took Alisa by the hand and made his way over to them. Inwardly, he let out a deep sigh of relief.

I-I maaade it! I actually made it through!

Until moments ago, he’d looked completely at ease on the dance floor, but in truth, he’d been barely holding it together.

What had him at his limit…? Well, it was Alisa’s , which, because they were dancing, he’d had no choice but to get blasted by at close range. No, he wasn’t being full of himself, and this definitely wasn’t a case of some adolescent virgin getting the wrong idea. And what’s more, she’d been smiling like that the whooole time.

He could feel her complete trust through their joined hands and the way their bodies stayed close as they danced. It was almost as if she’d been showing him how much she cared the entire time without ever saying a word. He could’ve sworn there were even little hearts floating deep in those blue eyes of hers. More than once, he’d found himself thinking, You’re not even trying to hide it anymore, are you?!

Alisa was already unbelievably beautiful, but somehow she looked even more captivating than usual, and the way she kept gazing at him so warmly was almost too much to handle. Even Masachika was struggling desperately to keep his cool. Regularly dealing with the sweet things she whispered to him in Russian had taught him to keep a poker face, and that was the only reason he’d managed to endure it. Otherwise, he never would have survived!

【That was amazing♡】

He didn’t even have to look at her to know. Alisa was probably watching him with that lovestruck look in her eyes and a little smile that practically said, “Heh, you still have no idea what I’m saying, do you?”

【Hey, why don’t we sneak out of here?】

Too fast, way too fast.

Besides, with her making it this obvious, everyone here is gonna catch on too, aren’t they…

Curious, he glanced around at the others. The students were all excitedly talking among themselves about the dance the two pairs had just performed, and from what he could tell, nobody seemed to be gossiping about them.

Well, it was different for me since I was right there taking the full force of it, but maybe it just wasn’t that noticeable from a distance? As that thought crossed his mind, Touya and the others smiled and called out to them.

“You two were really good out there. Honestly, I didn’t expect you to dance that well.”

“Alya-chan, you looked absolutely stunning! And Kuze-kun, I didn’t know you could dance that well either! Man, now I’m feeling the pressure, having to go after that.”

“You two were amaaazing! Big Sis is getting all emotional!!”

Masachika and Alisa smiled back, looking a little bashful as the three upperclassmen praised them.

“Thank you very much. I’m just glad our first dance turned out to be something we could be proud of.”

“Are you and Sarashina-senpai dancing next, President?”

Alisa had apparently finally made her way out of whatever flower field she’d been lost in. Masachika quietly breathed a sigh of relief when she responded like her usual self. Chisaki simply nodded with a smile, seemingly oblivious to everything that had just happened.

“Yeah, that was the plan… or at least, that’s what I was going to say, but it looks like the music’s already started! Well, Touya, shall we?”

“Ah… yeah. Let’s go!”

After psyching himself up, Touya led Chisaki onto the dance floor. Several other students, each paired up with a partner, also began making their way forward.

Hm? Is that…

Among them, Masachika spotted two familiar upperclassmen who had once looked out for him: Kaji Taiki, from his old junior-high student council, and Asama Kirika, its former vice president. Seeing the two of them together, Masachika’s eyes widened in surprise.

Half a year ago, Taiki had lost the student council election to Touya, which had led to him and Kirika breaking up. After that, he’d gotten mixed up in the Shurei Festival incident Yuushou had incited and received a pretty harsh scolding from Yuki for it… or at least, that was what Masachika had heard.

Those two… did they somehow end up getting back together after all?

Masachika watched in surprise as Taiki held out a hand to Kirika, inviting her onto the dance floor. Kirika took it with a distant look, as though she were doing so reluctantly. Looking at them, it was hard to believe they’d actually made up, but…

Yep. They definitely made up.

Masachika knew this was simply how they had always been. Kirika had always been headstrong and hard to deal with, while Taiki was the gentleman who patiently and kindly put up with her.

Maybe Kirika-senpai had actually been waiting all this time for the student council president to come after her.

He was relieved to see that the two people he had once admired as President and Vice President hadn’t changed at all. His attention then shifted back to the pair before him. Facing each other, the tall, slender beauty and the strong, dependable man at her side certainly made a striking pair.

Still, one thought crossed his mind.

“Do you think the President can actually dance…? I dunno, I just can’t really picture it,” Masachika said.

“In that case, I can’t really picture Sarashina-senpai dancing either…”

“Chisaki-chan isn’t gonna start swinging the President around, is she~?” Masha teased.

“As in… physically?”

“This isn’t pro wrestling…” Alisa muttered.

As Masachika chatted with the Kujo sisters, the dance began, and on the very first step, Touya’s feet left the floor.

“““……””” The three of them just stared.

Touya and Chisaki kept dancing as though nothing had happened, while Masachika and the Kujo sisters were left speechless.

“…He floated for a second there, didn’t he?”

“…Yeah, he came off the ground,” Masachika replied.

“It was just like seeing a magic trick, wasn’t it?”

As the three of them quietly tried to make sense of what they’d just seen, a male student came over to Maria.

“Good evening, Maria-san.”

“Good evening, Andou-kun,” Maria replied casually.

“…Andou-senpai?!” Masachika blurted out.

“W-Why are you acting so surprised?”

“Ah, no…” Masachika muttered.

Masachika kept looking at Andou-senpai, feeling like it had been ages since he’d last seen him. After a second, though, he realized there was really nothing strange about him being there and awkwardly looked away.

Andou seemed a little puzzled by his underclassman’s reaction, but soon turned his attention back to Maria, complimenting her on how she was dressed for the party before looking around for something.

“By the way… are you here by yourself today, Maria-san?”

“Yeah, just me today.”

“Then… if you’d like, would you care to dance with me?”

Andou gave a slight bow with a smile, and Maria smiled back, her brows lowering slightly in apology.

“Sorry. I’m really happy you asked, but I have to leave soon. There’s something important I need to take care of…”

“A-Ah… I see. Well, if that’s the case, I guess there’s no helping it.”

“Thanks. Maybe another time.”

Maria turned him down with a smile. Andou, however, was not only one of the most popular guys at the academy, but also a master at getting rejected by girls. He knew better than to press the issue and smoothly took his leave.

Watching from the corner of his eye, Masachika thought with admiration, As expected of Masha-san, she really is popular… but this was hardly the time to be worrying about someone else’s business.

“Hey, Kuze. That dance earlier was amazing.”

“Huh? Oh… thanks.”

“Seriously, though, I’m surprised. I never knew you were that good at dancing.”

The person who had approached him was a second-year student from the basketball club whom Masachika knew. Though a little caught off guard by his upperclassman’s sudden approach, Masachika responded anyway, only for the upperclassman to glance over at Alisa before continuing.

“So, uh… would it be okay if I asked Kujou-san to dance?”

“!”

Masachika instinctively looked over at Alisa. Her eyes widened slightly when she met his gaze, but she quickly looked away and muttered under her breath.

【No…】

Gulp. Masachika swallowed hard as Alisa lightly tugged at the hem of his clothes and mumbled again.

【You’re the only one who’s allowed to touch me…】

Gghk?!

The sheer destructive power of those words nearly sent Masachika’s eyes rolling back in his head… Then, as he watched the situation unfold, he realized there was a major problem. But by then, it was already too late.

Hm? Wait, this… this is bad, isn’t it? No, this is really bad!!

It felt as though a bucket of cold water had been dumped over his head, and he could feel the blood draining from his face. Masachika now realized the problem: his partner couldn’t dance with any other boys, a serious handicap for an election candidate at a dance party.

It went without saying that turning down an invitation to dance at a party would hurt the other person’s pride, at least to some extent. Of course, people did sometimes turn down invitations with an excuse, like Maria had. But unlike Maria, Alisa was a candidate in the election.

Considering the election campaign ahead, there was almost no way they could turn him down here. After all, the fact that he had come to Alisa and Masachika before Yuki and Ayano meant there was a good chance he was already one of their more enthusiastic supporters. Sending him away without any real reason would be like tearing up a vote that had just been handed to them. But…

Alya’s not the kind of person who’d be comfortable with that… There’s no way she’d dance with a guy she barely knows…!

And if he was being completely honest… Masachika didn’t want Alisa dancing with another guy either. Still, when he thought about the election…

Damn it, no! She’s gotta dance with him! But I can’t just make Alya do something she doesn’t want to… Wait, was this Yuki’s plan all along?!

Only then did the possibility finally occur to him. Yuki was the one who had planned this party in the first place. She had to know that Alisa wouldn’t want to dance with other boys. If Alisa turned down the dance just like she expected, it wouldn’t be long before she had a line of people waiting to dance with her while Alisa was left standing off to the side like a Anyone who saw that would naturally think Yuki was the more popular of the two.

And if everyone goes into winter break with that impression still fresh in their minds… then no one’s going to remember how close things were at the closing ceremony.

It took Masachika about three seconds to work all that out, and another second to decide what to do.

Daaamn it, I’ve got no choice. I’ll have to play the possessive boyfriend and make it look like I was the one who wouldn’t let Alya dance with another guy, then shift the focus onto me instead…

With that, Masachika turned back to the upperclassman in front of him to reject his offer in a joking manner, but then…

“Oh, excuse me? I actually called dibs on dancing with Alissa before you did~”

Masachika and the basketball player both turned toward the voice beside them. There stood Nonoa, her distinctive blond hair tied back in a ponytail and draped over one shoulder, dressed in a black tailcoat.

“Right, Alissa?”

“Y-yes, that’s right.”

Under Nonoa’s watchful eyes, Alisa blinked repeatedly before nodding. Masachika was equally shocked by Nonoa’s sudden intervention, but he immediately decided to play along.

“Sorry, senpai. You heard what she said…”

“Ah, r-right. Well, in that case, I guess it can’t be helped…”

The rejected student stood back, staring intently at Alisa and Nonoa, apparently startled by the appearance of a blonde beauty in men’s formalwear.

“Well then, shall we go?”

“Huh? But the song isn’t over yet…”

“No worries, no worrries~!”

The moment she finished speaking, Nonoa took Alisa by the hand, guided her into an empty spot, and began dancing with her.

“Hey, look at those two…”

“Huh? Whoaa! That’s right, Kujou-san and Miyamae-san have an alliance!”

The two girls were both famous throughout the school, and seeing them dance together once again drew plenty of attention from those around them. As Masachika watched, he breathed a small sigh of relief.

Well, I’m not sure how I feel about Nonoa coming to our rescue, but at least that bought us some time…

Masachika remained on guard around Nonoa, unsure whether she was friend or foe at this point, as he checked on the other students who were dancing.

The president and Sarashina-senpai seem to be doing fine on the dance floor for now. There’s Ayano… Wait, is she partnered with someone from class? And Yuki… Huh? She’s not dancing?

Ayano was dancing with a girl who was clearly enjoying herself, though she was struggling a little to keep up. Yuki, meanwhile, was surrounded by a number of boys but seemed content to talk with them rather than dance with anyone. Masachika raised an eyebrow, surprised to see Yuki acting so differently than he’d expected.

Knowing her, I thought she’d jump at the chance to accept dance invitations and show everyone how much more sociable she is than Alya… Or was I just overthinking it earlier? Maybe she’s leaving the dancing to Ayano so she can spend that time making connections instead?

While Masachika was still trying to make sense of it all, he heard a familiar girl’s voice beside him.

“Good evening, Kuze-san.”

“Oh, Saya—ka…”

Masachika turned toward the voice, only to fall silent when he saw her. She seemed to have picked up on his reaction, furrowing her brows with a slightly confrontational look before pushing up her glasses.

“Is something the matter?”

“No… I just think your hair looks great, is all?”

“…Is that so? Well, thank you,” Sayaka replied, her expression unchanged.

With the ends of her hair permed and a braid woven into the right side, she looked noticeably different. It was nothing like her usual plain short haircut, and even Masachika was taken aback, wondering what had made her change her appearance so much.

“Did you go out of your way to style your hair like that just for today’s party?”

“…No, it’s not like that.”

“???”

Masachika thought for a moment, wondering what else it could possibly be…

…Huh? Hmm? No way. Wait, could it be?

Seeing Sayaka looking restless as she stumbled across her words and averted her gaze, Masachika followed a sudden hunch and glanced around.

“…Is Takeshi not with you today?”

“!!! Why would you bring Takeshi-san into this all of a sudden?!”

Sayaka immediately looked up, reacting far more strongly than necessary, to which Masachika raised both hands in a calming gesture and replied with, “Well, I just thought Takeshi would have wanted to enter with you as his partner…”

“…As you might have guessed, Nonoa is my partner for today’s event.”

“O-oh, I see.”

There were plenty of things he wanted to ask, but Masachika decided that pressing her on the matter would probably only complicate things. He swallowed his questions and shifted his attention towards Alisa and Nonoa, who were dancing together surprisingly well despite being a little awkward, before speaking in a quiet voice.

“…Thanks. You really helped me out.”

Although his words felt like an empty thank you, Sayaka seemed to understand exactly what he meant and replied curtly.

“You seem to be mistaken about something, but that was Nonoa’s decision alone. I had nothing to do with it.”

“I-is that so?”

“That’s right. As I’ve told you before, I’m neutral when it comes to the election campaign itself.”

“……”

For someone who claimed to be neutral, Sayaka certainly seemed to be helping them out quite a bit, but if she said so, then she really must have been uninvolved in this particular incident.

So Nonoa anticipated that Alya would be in trouble because she couldn’t dance with other guys, and deliberately came dressed in men’s formalwear…? Honestly, I’m grateful for the help, but what exactly is she planning?

Masachika didn’t fully believe Nonoa had done this out of the goodness of her heart. He kept a careful eye on the two girls, suspicious of her motives, and noticed they were discussing something.

Wonder what they're talking about?

Masachika furrowed his brows, raising his alertness even further, but the dance ended without anything in particular happening afterward. Even so, he decided he should go pick Alisa up sooner rather than later, just to be safe…

Huh?!

For some reason, Nonoa wasn’t bringing Alisa back to him and instead headed somewhere else with her. Masachika stopped for a moment and then it happened.

“Ahhh!!”

A male student’s voice rang out, sounding almost like a panicked scream. Overlapping with it came the sharp, brittle crash of shattering glass. The sounds erupted as the music stopped, almost as if it was timed perfectly, drawing the attention of everyone in the gymnasium. What they saw was a serving tray lying on the floor, shards of glass scattered everywhere, and Alisa and Nonoa standing nearby with their clothes stained by the spilled drinks.

“I-I’m so sorry! I’m really, really sorry!”

A male student with glasses and wearing a vest, presumably the one who had been carrying the broken glasses, bowed deeply and apologized to the two girls. As Masachika and Maria hurried over, Nonoa looked down at her stained trousers and let out a little “Ah~”.

“Well, if it wasn’t on purpose, it’s totally fine, but… we should probably wash these before the stains set in… especially Alisa’s dress. Mine’s black, so it’s no big deal.”

“Ah, um, well, yes. Oh, you don’t have to apologize so much… Please, lift your head.”

Alisa finally recovered from the shock of what had just happened and spoke to the boy. He was still bowing, looking as though he might drop into at any moment. By that point, Yuki and Masachika had arrived.

“I’m sorry, are you alright—”

“You okay, Aly—” Masachika began.

Yuki, who was in charge of the party, and Masachika, Alisa’s partner, were both about to speak up. But before either could say anything, a group of female students appeared out of nowhere and quickly surrounded Alisa and Nonoa.

“Your dress got stained?!” one of the girls exclaimed.

“What?! That’s an emergency!” another girl cried out.

“Let’s get those stains out! Right away!!”

“Do you need a change of clothes?! You must, right?!”

For all their talk of an emergency, the girls sounded strangely happy… or rather, they were clearly excited. They were from the Handicrafts Club, after all.

They never missed a chance to dress beautiful girls in clothes they’d made themselves. The students watching from a distance took one look at them and seemed to think, ‘Oh, here we go…’ Knowing what was coming, the students stepped aside without a word, leaving a clear path to the gymnasium doors.

“Come on, let’s go! The sooner we get those stains out, the better!” one of the girls urged.

“I’ll go on ahead and get everything ready!” another called out.

“Then I’ll get a change of clothes ready!” a third girl chimed in.

“Hey! Don’t try to get ahead of the rest of us!” a fourth girl protested.

With club members holding onto them from both sides, Alisa and Nonoa were escorted away. Though might be a more accurate description.

“Eh? W-wait, ehhh?! We’re still in the middle of the party—“

“Sorry, Kuzecchi~, I’m going to dip for a bit, so ask Sayacchi to be your partner in the meantime~”

Alisa looked to Masachika in confusion, as though pleading for his help. Meanwhile, Nonoa looked like she’d completely given up, yet she had no problem dropping an unreasonable request in his lap. Before anyone knew it, the two had been whisked away from the gymnasium.

“Everyone, I’m sorry for the commotion. As the person in charge of this party, please accept my sincere apologies.”

Yuki bowed alongside the boy who had dropped the glass, keeping him behind her as though to shield him. The students gathered around her were already assuring her that there was nothing to worry about. She acknowledged their reassurances with a smile while discreetly instructing the boy behind her to clean up the broken glass.

“Sorry, I’m sorry…”

With help from the other students working the event, the boy hurried to clean up, muttering apology after apology. As Masachika watched, he couldn’t help feeling suspicious about the whole thing.

That guy… Nonoa put him up to this, didn’t she?

Masachika hadn’t noticed anything unusual about the way the boy dropped the glass. But it had happened in the very spot Nonoa had steered Alisa toward, and the incident had given her an excuse to leave without dancing with any of the other boys. It certainly looked like Nonoa had arranged the whole thing to throw Alisa a lifeline.

And another thing, she’s made it look like the accident happened because someone on the organizing staff messed up, so Yuki would end up taking the blame. That’s pretty underhanded of her… Hm? Was this whole thing already arranged with the handicrafts club, too?

The handicrafts club had stepped in so quickly that Masachika briefly wondered if they were in on it too, but he dismissed the idea.

Nah, it’s probably just a coincidence. I can’t imagine Nonoa would be so willing to let other people in on her schemes.

Regardless, he had his reservations about Nonoa’s methods, but… there was no denying she’d helped him.

Without Nonoa getting Alisa out of there, another crowd of boys would’ve come rushing over to ask her to dance, and Masachika would’ve had his hands full trying to deal with them.

To think Nonoa would end up covering for me after I foolishly showed up at this dance party without a plan…

Between this and what had happened at the closing ceremony, it seemed he’d had tunnel vision lately. As Masachika reflected on this, Maria looked in the direction Alisa had gone and let out a drawn-out “Hmm~”

“Actually, this is perfect timing. Maybe I’ll head home too.”

“Oh, are you?”

“Yeah. I got to see Alya-chan and Chisaki-chan dance. Besides, I need to go get ready for the birthday party.”

“I see… Well, see you later, then.”

“Mm-hmm… Oh!” Maria leaned a little closer to Masachika, speaking softly in Russian.

【Though, it’s a shame we didn’t get to share a dance together, Kuze-kun】

“!”

“Fufu, I’ll see you later, then~” Maria said with a mischievous smile.

Maria left Masachika staring wide-eyed as she made her way out of the gymnasium, waving to Touya and Chisaki along the way. He watched her leave, doing his best to appear unfazed, then turned to Sayaka, who had been following behind him.

“So, about what Nonoa said earlier…”

“……”

Sayaka seemed to have her own thoughts about everything that had happened. She looked back at Masachika with a somewhat troubled expression, and he gave a small laugh and shrugged.

“Well, I can’t exactly ask you to be my partner, Sayaka. That wouldn’t work for a few different reasons,” he said, half to himself.

Masachika looked around and spotted Takeshi standing by himself near the wall a short distance away, then gestured for him to come over.

“…Eh? W-what’s up, Masachika?”

Takeshi approached hesitantly. “What’s he so nervous about?” Masachika thought to himself, somewhat put off by Takeshi’s reaction, then spoke to him directly.

“You saw that, right? Sayaka’s lost her partner, so go dance with her.”

“W-Wait, me?! But…” Takeshi hesitated.

“Want me to do it instead?” Masachika asked.

“Ah, no, it’s just…”

With Masachika egging him on, Takeshi went through a whole range of expressions over the next few seconds. Finally, he bowed his head and held out his right hand to Sayaka.

“P-Please!!”

“Stop that. You’re embarrassing me,” Sayaka said curtly, making Takeshi lower his outstretched arm.

“Honestly,” Sayaka sighed.

Before his hand could drop completely, Sayaka grabbed it and started walking briskly.

“Eh? Oh—S-See you later, Masachika!”

Takeshi disappeared into the crowd of students as Sayaka pulled him along. Masachika watched them go with mixed feelings, tilting his head slightly.

“…Looks like things are working out for those two after all, huh?”

Honestly, he’d thought Takeshi didn’t stand much of a chance with her, but judging by what he’d just seen, Sayaka wasn’t exactly rejecting him either. Still, since they hadn’t come to the party together, they probably weren’t dating yet, though there did seem to be something between them…

Did the two of them get closer on their date? Actually, wasn’t that when Sayaka changed her hairstyle too?

Masachika never got the full story about Takeshi and Sayaka’s date, which they’d arranged after Takeshi got carried away and confessed to her in front of everyone. He knew they’d gone, but when he’d asked Takeshi how it went, he’d only said, “It went alright, I guess?” So Masachika decided not to press him any further.

…Well, as long as things are going well between them, that’s good enough for me. Good luck, Takeshi.

Masachika silently cheered on his friend in his efforts to win Sayaka’s heart when a woman’s clear, dignified voice called out from beside him.

“Good evening, Kuze-san.”

“Vio… Likewise, Sumire-senpai.”

Her cousin Yuushou stood behind her, though… he looked more like her attendant than her partner.

…And he’s supposed to be the one running for student council president?

Masachika was still trying to make sense of Sumire having the upper hand over Yuushou when she gracefully offered him her hand.

“May I have this dance?”

“?!”

It wasn’t Masachika who looked the most shocked, but Yuushou. Sure, Masachika was surprised too, but catching a glimpse of Yuushou’s stunned expression out of the corner of his eye actually helped him regain his composure.

I mean, he did my hair for me, so I owe him one, and I really don’t want to pull something straight out of an NTR… But then again, considering the election campaign, I can’t really justify turning her down.

For a moment, Masachika wondered if he should hold back for Yuushou’s sake, but the thought didn’t stick around long enough to get any further than that.

“With pleasure,” Masachika replied.

Masachika smiled and took Sumire’s hand without showing even a hint of hesitation. He noticed Yuushou staring daggers at their joined hands, but he wasn’t going to let that bother him. Not one bit.

“So you really are my rival…!!”

Nope, still not bothered. Not one bit!

“Whoa, it’s Sumire-senpai!”

“Wait, is she going to dance with Kuze…?!”

“So Kiryuuin-san really is backing Kujou-san and Kuze-san…!”

As Masachika and Sumire began to dance, the students around them buzzed with excitement at the sight of yet another pair worth watching.

With her striking looks and equally impressive dress, Sumire carried herself with the confidence and poise you’d expect. Her dancing, though, was more traditional, showing a firm grasp of the basics.

They started with measured steps, matching each other’s timing. Once they found their rhythm, they gradually began adding touches of their own without getting in each other’s way. If their partner took the cue, all they had to do was go with the flow. And since they were both experienced dancers, they moved through each stage without missing a beat.

“Oh, you’re better than I thought.”

“You’ve still got me beat, Sumire-senpai.”

“Fufu, and you know how to give a compliment, too.”

They continued their playful exchange as they danced slowly to the music. There was nothing particularly showy about their dancing, but they were clearly a step above the rest, and the students around them voiced their admiration.

“…Thanks, you really helped me out there,” Masachika said, dancing as if he were on autopilot.

“Well, hearing you thank me like that makes it all worth it,” Sumire replied with a pleased smile.

“Honestly, I wasn’t sure what to do when I ended up alone…” Masachika explained. “And I doubt many students would’ve approached me, either.”

Masachika wasn’t just saying that. He could have used his way with words to make connections on his own, but he couldn’t compete with Yuki’s reputation or charm.

Alisa attracted attention just like Yuki did, but it was the goal she’d announced in her closing ceremony speech that had everyone talking. No one had ever proposed anything like it before. Even without her, Masachika could still have talked to people, but he’d have been the one going up to people, not the other way around.

“Come now, you’re not giving yourself nearly enough credit…”

“Eh?”

“Oh, it’s nothing. Then how about I be your partner until Kujou-san gets back?”

“Well, that’s—”

But where does that leave Yuushou, her partner? The question was gone almost as soon as it crossed Masachika’s mind. Still, he could at least give himself credit for hesitating longer this time.

“…Then could I take you up on that?” Masachika asked.

“Sure, I’d be happy to join you,” Sumire replied.

“Heh…”

Sumire’s reply made Masachika feel he could count on her. He smiled faintly, then asked a question that got to the heart of it all.

“But why… are you willing to go this far for us?” Masachika asked.

“Why, it’s because I like Alisa-san of course.”

Masachika hadn’t expected her to reply right away and almost stopped dancing, but quickly caught himself.

“Alisa-san’s speech at the closing ceremony deeply moved me. She was so earnest and confident about pursuing a goal some might call unrealistic. The last person whose way of life had such an effect on me was… Onee-sama.”

“By Onee-sama… do you mean Sarashina-senpai?”

Masachika’s eyes widened in surprise at how much Alisa’s speech had meant to Sumire.

“So I’ve decided to support Alisa-san. But just after I made up my mind, that accident happened. Surely you can understand why I’d want to help?”

“…Yeah, maybe.”

Sumire seemed to take the accident at face value, too trusting to consider that someone might have caused it on purpose.

Yuushou probably suspects it wasn’t an accident either… but whatever.

With that thought, he glanced toward Yuushou… and found him glaring straight at him. Seeing that, Masachika turned back as if he hadn’t noticed.

When the song ended, Masachika escorted Sumire back to where they’d been standing, careful not to meet Yuushou’s gaze. Whether or not she noticed Masachika’s discomfort, Sumire made an offhand but cruel remark to Yuushou.

“Yuushou-san, I’ll be accompanying Kuze-san until Alisa-san gets back, so why don’t you find something to do for a while?”

“Eh——”

Yuushou had a look of shock on his face, but Sumire delivered another blow just as nonchalantly.

“If you want, you can just leave without me, you know?”

From the way she said it, Yuushou knew he was just the closest boy she could dance with.

“…I’m going to get some air,” Yuushou said, then turned away, his shoulders slumped.

That was all he said before heading for the gym doors. He looked so defeated as he walked away that Masachika, as a guy himself, couldn’t help feeling sorry for him.

“Let’s see… Why don’t we go say hello to the second-years I know first?”

“…Sure. Lead the way.”

Sumire didn’t seem at all bothered that Yuushou left. Masachika took his cue from her and turned his thoughts elsewhere. By now, she was the one leading the way as they went over to where a few second-years had gathered.

“Hello, everyone,” Sumire said to the group.

“Hey, Sumire-san. I’m surprised you’d actually dance with him.”

“Kiryuuin-san, seeing you here with him… should we take that to mean you’re supporting Kujou-san and Kuze-san?” one of the second-years asked.

“Yes, that’s exactly what I’m saying.”

Sumire had made it clear whose side she was on, and that caused a bit of a stir among the students present.

“Oh!” another student said. “What do you like about those two, Kiryuuin-san?”

“You can tell us over here,” another student added.

People kept coming over, and before Masachika knew it, he and Sumire were surrounded by very sociable students, most of them second-years.

Huh, I had a much harder time approaching people like this when it was just Alya and me…

While keeping such thoughts to himself, he got to know the students around him little by little. Some had looked down on him at first, seeing him as little more than someone tagging along with Alisa or Sumire. But Masachika had grown up as the Suou family’s heir, so he’d had plenty of practice talking to people of higher status.

“That’s a really nice watch, Senpai. The face looks just like a starry sky, doesn’t it?”

“Hm? Oh, this?”

As soon as Masachika brought up the watch, Sumire slipped right into the conversation.

“You’re right. It really is beautiful. What brand is it?”

“It’s not from a fancy brand or anything… I went to see a show at a planetarium once and picked it up at the gift shop there.”

“Oh, so that’s where you got it! Do you like planetariums?”

With Sumire’s help, Masachika soon found it easy to join in on the upperclassmen’s conversations.

Communication is a skill. Some people have a natural gift for drawing attention and getting others to like them, but with effort and experience, even an ordinary person can get by to a certain extent.

His grandfather, Gensei, had drilled that into him when he was younger. Two people with a certain level of education and refinement could always find something to talk about, as long as they minded their manners and steered clear of touchy subjects. But…

“By the way, Kuze, where did you get that suit?”

There were still people who would ask an unpleasant question on purpose, even when they already knew the answer.

"This one? It’s , always a safe bet. I’m just a commoner, so I wear this to pretty much every formal occasion, from weddings to funerals. I don’t have a suit made for a fancy party like this. Then again, are expensive suits really that different from mass-produced ones?”

Masachika didn’t take offense or let the question rattle him. He brushed it off with a casual answer, and Sumire stepped in to back him up right away.

“Of course, a custom suit differs from one off the rack in quite a few ways. It can have a more elegant silhouette, feel more comfortable, and be easier to move in. But… whatever the outfit, it’s the person wearing it who matters. Even the most expensive clothes can look awkward or cheap on someone who lacks refinement, and someone with real elegance can make even ordinary clothes look magnificent.”

At the same time, she lightly scolded the classmate who’d made the snide remark.

“Exactly! I shine just as brightly whether I’m in a dress or my school uniform.”

She finished with a bold claim that could’ve been a joke or entirely serious statement. Either way, she said it with enough confidence to lighten the mood.

Hahaha. She’s incredible. No wonder everyone around looks up to her.

Sumire had made a lasting impression on Masachika. As he continued walking through the gym, he eventually saw Yuki step onto the stage and begin her closing remarks.

“Ladies and gentlemen, I apologize for interrupting while you’re all enjoying yourselves. As much as we hate to see this wonderful evening end, it’s nearly time to bring the event to a close.”

Voices of disappointment rose from several parts of the gym. Yuki smiled at their reaction and continued.

“Thank you for expressing such heartfelt disappointment. The tremendous success of our very first event is thanks to everyone who accepted our invitation and joined us tonight. Above all, it’s thanks to the many people who volunteered their time and effort as part of the organizing staff. I’d like everyone here tonight to join me in giving our staff a big round of applause. Thank you all so very much!”

Yuki bowed deeply to the staff gathered below the stage, then began clapping. Soon the entire gym joined in. Once the applause died down, Yuki spoke again.

“Now then, the next song will be the final one of the evening. It will be our last dance. So, everyone, please enjoy yourselves until the very—”

“Excuse me~! Could you please make way for us?!”

A female student’s voice suddenly rang out, cutting Yuki’s speech short.

Many students turned toward the voice with disapproving looks. It had come from the gym entrance directly opposite the stage. Their displeasure vanished the moment they caught sight of the girls standing there. One after another, the students near the entrance stepped aside to clear a path for them.

“Alya…”

Alisa Kujou and Nonoa Miyamae, the two girls who’d left partway through the party, stepped into view along the path the crowd had just cleared. Behind them, the Handicrafts Club members stood in a row with their arms crossed, posing like mentors watching their pupils.

But both girls returned in outfits completely different from what they’d been wearing before. Nonoa had traded her black tailcoat for a gorgeous dress. And as though they’d switched roles, Alisa was the one dressed as a man this time.

“Whoaaa, she looks so cool…”

“She’s the very picture of a beauty in menswear…”

“Beautiful…”

As voices of admiration echoed through the crowd like ripples, the Handicrafts Club members watched with smug expressions as Alisa, clad in a pure-white knight’s uniform, escorted Nonoa forward.

It was such a magnificent sight that one might have thought the gymnasium had suddenly transformed into a Western castle. Yuki resumed her speech with a somewhat wry smile.

“…Well then, now that we’ve been graced with the appearance of such a beautiful knight and princess… Allow me to say once again that this will be the final dance of the evening. Everyone, please enjoy it to the very end.”

Yuki finished speaking and bowed, and warm applause filled the gym. Alisa, meanwhile, reached the center of the floor and stopped. Nonoa looked around the room before fixing her eyes on Masachika.

Is she for real?

The thought had barely crossed his mind when Nonoa split off from Alisa and headed his way, as if to prove him right. Alisa went straight to the stage and met Yuki as she stepped down.

Ahh~ so that’s how it is.

Masachika knew instinctively what was about to happen. He excused himself with an “I’ll be right back” to Sumire and the second-years gathered around him, then made his way through the crowd to meet Nonoa.

“Hey, Kuzecchi. Wanna dance?”

“…I’d be happy to.”

Masachika put on a friendly face and took Nonoa’s hand. He caught a glimpse of Alisa, dressed as a knight, asking Yuki to dance. She took Alisa’s hand and gave her what looked like a friendly smile.

Up to that point, everything had gone just as Masachika had expected… that is, until he took Nonoa’s hand and led her toward the center of the gym. Ayano of all people stepped into view between the other students, leading Sayaka by the hand.

“……”

Masachika turned to Nonoa, silently asking, “Did you plan this too?” She glanced back at him and gave a little shrug. “I mean, how would it look if Ayanono was the only one we left out?”

“…Fair point.”

Masachika had plenty of questions for Nonoa, like how she’d talked Sayaka into it and whether she just wanted to keep Takeshi and Sayaka from sharing the last dance. But she did have a point… In fact, it was a really considerate thing to say, so he just swallowed his words and nodded.

“Whoa, now that’s a last dance!”

“Nobody else is going out there when it’s like this…” another student added.

“W-Would it be okay if I filmed this?”

Once the three pairs were in position on the floor, the music started as if someone had timed it perfectly. Masachika had wondered if Nonoa would take the dance seriously. When she began to dance, she wasn’t particularly graceful, but she was careful with her steps and didn’t try anything risky.

“…Nonoa.”

“Hmm?”

“…Thanks. You really saved me today.”

As they danced, Masachika figured Nonoa didn’t have any ulterior motives, at least for now.

“Oh, don’t mention it, Kuzecchi. I’m supposed to be helping you and Alissa anyway, so it’s not a big deal.”

“……”

Even so, her blatantly insincere response caused him to frown a little. Nonoa seemed to see right through him and laughed under her breath.

“No need to be sooo wary of me. Saying that probably won’t help, but believe it or not, I really do plan to support you two in the election, y’know?”

“…And why’s that?”

Nonoa’s smile widened at Masachika’s direct question.

“I told ya before, didn’t I? I wanna see something that’ll surprise me. I heard Alissa’s speech today and figured she’d keep me guessing if she won. It’s that simple.”

“……”

“With Yukki, it felt like things would go smoothly, which is kinda a double-edged sword, y’know… Sure, it’s something new, but if anything happens, it’s only a small hiccup. So I don’t see things getting messy, do ya?”

Masachika said nothing as he tried to figure out what Nonoa was really after. She smiled at him, and he half expected her to lick her lips.

“I figured Alissa’s campaign pledge would make things interesting either way. She might actually pull it off and go down in history, or she could fail miserably and have to live with that humiliation, that works too.”

“…Makes sense.”

Even coming from Nonoa, what she said made sense. If she’d said she was doing this because of her friendship with Alisa or because she wanted to make amends for betraying her, Masachika would’ve had a hard time taking her at her word. The fact that he could believe her this time was exactly what bothered him.

I can never tell what’s going through her head or what drives her… and now she gives me a reason I can actually follow and agree with? That alone makes me doubt her. I’d sooner believe she just told me something that sounded truthful enough to convince me.

Still, at this point Masachika had nothing to refute her, and if he wasn’t careful about letting his suspicions show, it could backfire and cause trouble.

“I really hope you mean that.”

That was why Masachika had no choice but to say what he did. Nonoa smiled as if she knew what he was thinking, then glanced to the side.

“Okay, now that’s settled. About time we switched.”

“Wha—?”

“See ya~”

Ignoring his confused reaction, Nonoa abruptly let go of his hand and turned away from him, heading toward Alisa and Yuki. A moment later, Yuki noticed and left Alisa to join Ayano. Then Sayaka came over to Masachika from where she’d been dancing with Ayano.

Ah… I was trying to avoid dancing with her for Takeshi’s sake, but here I am anyway.

Smiling wryly to himself, Masachika took Sayaka’s hand and got into position. Then, matching her rhythm, he began to dance…

“Ngh?!” Masachika winced in pain.

“Oops.”

Sayaka’s first step landed right on his toes.

I’m a gentleman, I’m a gentleman, I’m a gentleman, I’m a gentleman…

Masachika put everything he had into being a gentleman and somehow managed to bear it.

“Let’s try again. Ready, and—”

He somehow kept his expression in check and eased back into the steps without making a sound that might give him away.

“One-two-three, one-two-three…”

Remembering what his dance instructor had taught him years ago, he counted softly and used his movements to guide Sayaka. Once they’d managed to find a steady rhythm, Masachika smiled at her.

“So even you have things you’re bad at, Sayaka.”

“…Of course I do,” Sayaka answered curtly, glancing down at their feet again.

She probably wasn’t in a bad mood, though. Just keeping up with him required all the focus she could muster.

Masachika was seeing a new side of Sayaka, and he smiled as he continued speaking.

“Fair enough. Sorry for getting you involved in this.”

“…It’s fine, I only did it because Nonoa asked me to.”

Sayaka looked like she had no attention to spare for the conversation, and an underhanded thought flashed through Masachika’s mind. Would she answer honestly if I asked about her and Takeshi right now? It’d be tactless to ask, and a friend who’d helped him out deserved better than that, so he dismissed the thought then and there.

After that, he concentrated on making it easier for Sayaka to dance. When the timing was right, he let go, and the two bowed to each other and parted.

Now then…

After parting ways with Sayaka, Masachika turned and locked eyes with Yuki as she approached. He smiled wryly at the happy gleam in her eyes as he took her hand, and the two began dancing.

“You really did it this time, huh.”

“The same could be said for you, my brother~”

“That was Nonoa’s doing,” Masachika pointed out.

Anyone listening might not have understood what was going on, but the two of them understood each other with just that short exchange.

“Hey, check those two out.”

“They’re totally in sync, right…?”

“Well, they are the former president and vice president…”

The two moved together with such finesse that even the students, who’d grown harder to impress after watching so many dances, couldn’t help but take notice. All the while, they continued speaking casually to each other in hushed voices.

“You should’ve known Alya-san wouldn’t be able to dance with a guy she wasn’t even friends with just to win votes, onii-chan. That’s on you for not seeing that coming and doing something about it.”

“…I guess you’ve got a point.”

Masachika was in no position to argue with her. He’d let his guard down and had no one to blame but himself. Nonoa had covered for him with a plan to leave partway through and dress Alya as a man, and he had to thank her for it.

“You’re one to talk. You’ve barely danced either, you know?”

Yuki had danced only twice, the first dance and this last one. Ayano, meanwhile, had somehow ended up dancing the whole time, with one girl after the next asking her to join them.

Masachika had expected Yuki to accept any invitation and use the opportunity to show Alisa just how much better she was at socializing, and he couldn’t help but be surprised by it all. Yuki looked up, then awkwardly avoided his gaze.

“Ah~, I guess that was a miscalculation on my part too…”

“?”

Before Masachika could ask Yuki what she meant, the song began drawing to a close, and he shifted his attention back to the dance. He made it through to the end, then bowed to the audience as loud applause rang out.

All at once, the three pairs began to hear loud cheers and praise from the crowd. Masachika smiled in response, and just as he let go of Yuki’s hand—

“Anyway... give it your all.”

With those parting words, Yuki turned and headed over to Ayano. Masachika watched her go, puzzled by what she'd said, when someone suddenly grabbed his left shoulder from behind.

“?!” Masachika turned to see who had grabbed him, only to find an unfamiliar second-year boy staring at him with bloodshot eyes.

“Kuzeee… You know what’s coming, don’t you…?!”

... Eh? Wait, wh-what’s going on?

Before Masachika could figure out what was going on, someone grabbed his right shoulder this time… and tightened their grip.

“He got between them, he got between them, he got between them, he got between them, he got between them.”

“Eep!”

When Masachika turned around, he found a boy with a crazed look in his eyes, chanting “He got between them” over and over like Behind him stood a whole line of boys, all staring with their eyes wide open.

“We shall show no mercy for any guy who gets between a yuri couple.”

And so Masachika learned the hard way why Yuki hadn’t danced with anyone… no, why she hadn’t been able to.
